newsitem.title: UK: UK's Chiroscience revenues, R&D spend rise.
newsitem.headline: UK's Chiroscience revenues, R&D spend rise.

text.p: British drug discovery company Chiroscience Group Plc said on Monday that its full-year operating losses climbed by 61 percent to 21.0 million pounds ($34.1 million), reflecting an 84 percent rise in research and development spending to 22.2 million stg.

But the group, which hopes to have its first major product, the anaesthetic Levobupivacaine, on the market next year, said revenues also rose sharply, up 133 percent to 11.5 million stg, due to a strong performance by its technology services division, ChiroTech.
ChiroTech, which offers services to other drug companies, turned in its first-ever operating profit in the year ended February 28 of 1.2 million pounds after losing 0.9 million stg a year earlier.
Operating losses at the core pharmaceutical operations nearly doubled to 20.4 million stg from 10.4 million stg.

Chief executive John Padfield said Levobupivacaine was "on course for filing in Europe this December and in the USA next April." He said the company's drug programmes for cancer, asthma and arthritis had already started or were about to start clinical trials.

Chiroscience, which raised 41.3 million stg through a share issue, said it ended the financial year in a strong cash position, with cash and investments of 51.4 million stg. ($ = 0.616 British Pounds)
